claim.pdf_says: 8.3.3.6.4  General rules  [subordinate to 8.3.3.6 Figurative constant values; a peer of 8.3.3.6.1 General, 8.3.3.6.2 General format and 8.3.3.6.3 Syntax rules]
claim.markdown_says: ### 8.3.3.6.4 General rules   (ISO_COBOL.md line 6253) -- same level as its parent '### 8.3.3.6 Figurative constant values' (line 6152), while its peer is '#### 8.3.3.6.1 General' (line 6155)
claim.why_it_matters: 8.3.3.6.4 is transcribed at the same heading level as its own parent 8.3.3.6, so the general rules for figurative constants read as a sibling of Figurative constant values rather than a subclause of it. Its peers 8.3.3.6.2 and 8.3.3.6.3 are worse still (H2 at lines 6168 and 6227), so all four subclauses of 8.3.3.6 sit at three different levels.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds.

(1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is self-refuting against its own kind label: it concedes the markdown contains '### 8.3.3.6.4 General rules'. I confirmed it at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:6253, character-for-character identical to the PDF's printed '8.3.3.6.4   General rules', in exactly the right position -- immediately after syntax rule 4 ('Symbolic-character-1 shall be specified in the SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.') and immediately before 'ALL FORMATS'. Clause number, title, and placement in the linear text all match. No text was lost.

(2) THE PDF CARRIES NO HEADING-LEVEL INFORMATION TO LOSE. I rendered p.145 and p.144 at 300 dpi and looked at the glyphs. On p.144, '8.3.3.6.2   General format' and '8.3.3.6.3   Syntax rules'; on p.145, '8.3.3.6.4   General rules'. All three are set in identical bold type, at identical point size, at identical left margin, with the identical wide tab between number and title. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 does not typographically differentiate clause depth at all -- a depth-4 heading such as '8.3.3.6 Figurative constant values' looks the same as a depth-5 heading such as '8.3.3.6.4 General rules'. Hierarchy is conveyed by the dotted clause number and by nothing else, and the transcription reproduces that number exactly. A markdown '#' count is therefore an interpolation by the transcriber with no counterpart in the source; a mismatch in it cannot be a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy, because the PDF states no value for it.

(3) NO MEANING CHANGES. 'General rules' as a bare title is meaningless without its number; the number '8.3.3.6.4' is present and unambiguously places the clause under 8.3.3.6. Every cross-reference in the document navigates by clause number, not by heading depth -- e.g. ISO_COBOL.md:8222 cites '8.3.3.6, Figurative constant values, General rule 3', resolving purely on the number. No reader or tool that reads the number can be misled about the nesting.

(4) THE PREMISE OF A PER-PAGE DEFECT IS FALSE -- THIS IS A UNIFORM GLOBAL PROPERTY. Heading depth never tracks clause depth anywhere in this transcription. Counting every numbered heading in the file: depth-2 clauses appear as H2 192x and H3 35x; depth-3 as H2 276x, H3 508x, H4 17x; depth-4 as H2 162x, H3 620x, H4 24x; depth-5 as H2 118x, H3 128x, H4 41x. The sibling subclauses immediately preceding 8.3.3.6 behave identically -- '8.3.3.2.4 General rules' (line 5897), '8.3.3.4.4 General rules' (line 6034) and '8.3.3.5.4 General rules' (line 6120) are all H2, while their own '.1 General' peers are H3 or H4. The '### ' on 8.3.3.6.4 is thus an instance of a document-wide heading-normalization artifact, not a page-145 transcription error. Ledgering it as a p.145 finding would imply a localized defect that does not exist, and would license roughly 1,900 identical entries.

Incidental (checked, NOT a defect): the PDF's p.145 opens with the orphaned continuation 'with the following restrictions:'. That text is not absent -- it is correctly rejoined to its parent sentence at ISO_COBOL.md:6231, ahead of the page-145 anchor. Page 145 is content-complete.

If the heading-level inconsistency is worth addressing at all, it is a single global normalization pass over ISO_COBOL.md (derive '#' depth mechanically from the dot-count of the clause number), not a reconciliation finding against page 145.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading '8.3.3.6.4 General rules' is present and verbatim-correct at ISO_COBOL.md:6253, in the correct position. The PDF renders every clause heading -- depth 4 and depth 5 alike -- in identical bold type at identical size, so it encodes no heading level for the transcription to lose; hierarchy is carried entirely by the clause number, which is transcribed exactly. The sole difference is the markdown '#' count, a transcriber-interpolated formatting attribute, and it is inconsistent document-wide rather than on this page (depth-5 clauses appear as H2 118x, H3 128x, H4 41x across the file; the analogous '.4 General rules' subclauses at lines 5897, 6034 and 6120 are all H2). Track as an optional whole-file heading-depth normalization, not as a page-145 finding.
